newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Palestinian right of return sacred.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Palestinian right of return sacred.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Tuesday that Palestinian refugees had a "holy right" to return to homes they were forced to leave when the Jewish state was established in 1948.
"I say to everybody that the right of refugees is a holy right," Arafat told a crowd of about 500 Palestinians at a Gaza City conference on refugees.
"The refugees issue is an essential and national issue for Moslems and Christians," he said.
Palestinians say more than three million Palestinians are refugees or descendants of refugees displaced from their homes in British-ruled Palestine in 1948.
A United Nations resolution called on Israel to allow the refugees to return or to give them compensation for the property they lost.

Under a self-rule deal signed in 1993, Israel and the PLO agreed to negotiate the fate of those refugees when the sides begin negotiations on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip following an interim period of self-rule.
Previous right-wing Israeli governments have opposed the return of Palestinian refugees, viewing this as a threat to the survival of Israel as a Jewish state.
